subject: POC: integration clarifications — auth, routing, embeddings, rate-control
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@stellarml.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@stellarml.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — quick clarification items

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to have a short recap so our eng team can prepare. A few concrete things we need clarified before we start the POC next week: 

1) Auth model — we prefer short-lived service tokens that rotate via our secrets manager. Can Redwood support both API-key header and an OAuth2 client-credential flow? Any preferred header names or freshness requirements we should implement on our side?

2) Routing / deployment model — we will start with hosted Redwood but may move to Dedicated if throughput cost looks good. For canary traffic, we plan to send a 5% sample to Redwood for 72 hours. How do you recommend we express canary routing in the SDK / API? Is there a routing header or tag?

3) Embeddings + reranker — primary flow: embed ~300 candidate passages (embedding calls) then call a ranker generation endpoint for N-best outputs. Are there suggested batching patterns for embeddings versus generation to avoid head-of-line latency?

4) Rate limiting and retries — our infra will front Redwood through a proxy. We need guidance for 429 handling, expected rate-limit headers, and a recommended idempotency strategy for generate/stream calls. Do you expose Retry-After or other rate metadata?

We can send estimated QPS for the PoC once we confirm the above. Attaching our baseline integration checklist from infra.

— Carlos
VP Engineering, Stellar ML
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@stellarml.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — quick clarification items

Carlos — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (SE) + Marissa (AM) for next steps. Below are practical recommendations from our side with explicit implementation examples you can hand to your infra team.

AUTH
- We support both API key (recommended header: Authorization: Bearer <KEY>) and OAuth2 client-credentials. For POC, API keys are faster to provision; for Dedicated or long-run, we usually recommend OAuth2 + short-lived tokens.
- Token freshness: refresh before expiry; our control plane will return HTTP 401 when token is expired. No other special handshake required.

ROUTING / CANARY
- Canary: the simplest approach is to set a custom header X-Redwood-Traffic-Tag (values: canary, default, control). SDKs expose a routing.param you can set per-request. On hosted, our policy engine will route by that tag. For example: X-Redwood-Traffic-Tag: canary
- If you want percentage-based split from your proxy, send 5% with the canary header and leave the rest untagged. We can also create workspace-level routing rules if you prefer central control.

EMBEDDINGS vs GENERATION
- Embeddings: use batch embeddings endpoint. Send up to 256 vectors per request for best throughput; if you have ~300 candidates, split into two requests (200 + 100) to keep latency predictable.
- Generation / reranker: keep generation calls small and call with top-K candidates (we recommend K=16 for your initial POC). Use prefix caching for repeated prompts.

RATE LIMITS / RETRIES / IDEMPOTENCY
- Headers: hosted endpoints return standard rate headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch seconds). We also include Retry-After for 429 when applicable.
- 429 semantics: treat 429 as retryable if the response includes Retry-After; otherwise apply exponential backoff + jitter. For stream/long-poll generation endpoints, 429s are usually non-idempotent — avoid automatic retry of partial streams. Instead: record failure and retry the request as a fresh invocation with an idempotency key.
- Recommended backoff: start with base=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max=10s, plus full jitter. Example pseudo: sleep = random(0, min(max_backoff, base * (2^attempt)))
- Idempotency keys: include header Idempotency-Key with a value you control to de-duplicate retries on our side. Pattern we recommend: <customer>-<endpoint>-<unix_ts>-<random6>. E.g. stellar-generation-1691670720-4f3a9b. For one-off non-retryable streaming ops, add session markers and persist client-side state.
- Request IDs: propagate X-Request-ID or Redwood-Request-Id through proxies so we can correlate logs/traces. If your proxy rewrites IDs, include original id in X-Forwarded-Request-ID.

SUSTAINED vs BURST QUOTAS (POC guidance)
- For the hosted POC we can support up to ~200 QPS sustained for your project in our default plan with bursts up to ~600 qps for short periods — we should confirm with infra if you have higher peaks. For embeddings we suggest batching to keep token cost down.

NEXT STEPS / ACTIONS
- Carlos: share expected QPS by endpoint (embed vs generate) — target Tue 08/11.
- Dev: create POC API key + test workspace and share keys via the secure portal (we will not send keys over email).
- Marissa: will attach a mutual action plan and pricing note for Dedicated if you need committed throughput.

If you want, Dev and I can hop in for a short 30-minute call Thu to walk through sample requests and a quick test harness.

— Sean
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Carlos — adding a couple commercial items so we have a clean mutual action plan for the trial. Attached is a short MAP (mutual_action_plan_stellarml.xlsx) and the integration checklist. Highlights: 

- POC window: target 8/18–9/1 (two weeks) with a 5% canary for the first 72 hours.
- Test workspace: we will provision a test workspace and a time-limited API key by EOD Wed (we will send the provisioning link to your security contact via the secure portal).
- Committed throughput: if you need Dedicated, we can provide an initial reserved pool mapping (monthly commit + burst rules). Pricing action item after you share expected token/month.

Please confirm the POC dates and that your team is comfortable with our idempotency header approach (Idempotency-Key) and the X-Redwood-Traffic-Tag for canary routing.

— Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — confirmed. Quick answers from our side: 

- Expected POC QPS: generation peak ~120 QPS (short bursts to 200 for up to 30s), embeddings steady ~25 QPS (we will batch to 150 vectors per request).
- Canary ok: 8/18 start with 5% traffic for 72 hours.
- Auth: we'll start with API key for POC, plan to integrate OAuth2 for long-run.
- Idempotency and headers: we will implement Idempotency-Key and X-Request-ID propagation through our proxy; will also preserve original ID in X-Forwarded-Request-ID.

Action: I will upload a short traffic profile (QPS by endpoint + expected token counts) to the Drive link by EOD Tue. Please provision test workspace and API key and add Dev as the technical contact.

— Carlos
VP Engineering, Stellar ML
